candidate_decisions.reason: All six nominated branches land on focus words, and the coordinated absence of knowledge, guidance, an illuminating book, and light independently activates the bounded reading of a tightly contested argument without external orientation. The cord and wayfinding images remain analogical where the branch is not the ordinary sense.

The focus favor and inwardness meet the supplied 31:14 sequence of maternal carrying, repeated weakness, weaning, and gratitude. Every nominated focus or context branch is retained; unresolved context branches remain attributed, with no branch gloss or facet invented.

The supplied 31:16 trace connects the focus inward and knowledge words to a measured, tiny object enclosed in rock and brought forth by God. The relation survives as an attributed contextual reading, with its accountability inference and the packet's counter-reading bounded explicitly.

The paired focus terms for outwardness and inwardness meet the 31:18-19 face, gait, and voice sequence. The hidden-posture reading remains an attributed inference alongside the possibility that these are discrete conduct instructions.

The focus absence of guidance and book meets 31:21's explicit contrast between following what God sent down and following what was found upon the fathers. Focus branches and each attributed context trace are retained; the relation does not require identifying the two groups as exactly the same people.

findings.title: A tightly contested argument without an orienting standard
findings.claim: The focus describes a verbal dispute that can be heard as internally tightened yet without an external point of orientation: knowledge is absent, as are guidance and an illuminating book.
findings.mechanism: The verb for disputing carries the ordinary contest of words; its nominated cord branch adds an analogical image of tight twisting. The separate negated terms for knowledge, guidance, written text, and illumination supply the missing landmark, map, and beacon, changing the dispute from mere verbal activity into an argument with internal tension but no stated guide.
findings.reader_payoff: The missing grounds are not a flat list: together they leave the disputant without a marker, a route, or a light by which to orient the argument.
findings.containment: The cord, map, landmark, and beacon are bounded analogies from the supplied branches. The verse describes this disputant as lacking these grounds; it does not make every debate false or say that a book is literally a map.

epistemic.reason: The focus words and negations are explicit, while the tightly twisted cord and wayfinding relations are source-supported analogies rather than literal descriptions.

findings.title: Maternal labor beneath the received favor
findings.claim: The focus still names outward and inward favors; 31:14 gives the inward side an embodied dimension, as the child's received life rests on hidden maternal carrying, repeated weakness, and weaning, followed by a command to give thanks.
findings.mechanism: The focus favor word carries a bestowed benefit, while inwardness meets 31:14's carrying, twofold weakness, weaning, and gratitude. Their contact changes hidden blessing from only an imperceptible gift into a benefit whose visible result can contain another person's unseen bodily and relational cost.
findings.reader_payoff: Gratitude can look behind the finished benefit to the labor and dependence that made a life possible.
findings.containment: The parental sequence illustrates one bodily and relational dimension of inward favor; it does not define every hidden blessing as maternal labor or displace divine gifts. The inference that another person's cost is itself included is attributed, and the parental unit may exemplify obligation without fixing the focus pair's full scope.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 31:14 Arabic anchors and the HFT word coordinates align, but the context root, branch, and role labels remain an unbound attributed trace.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Favor can include a received good whose human cost is borne out of sight by another.
branch_activations.boundary: The sequence illustrates this relation without defining every favor or assigning a full theory of obligation.

findings.title: The hidden remains within reach
findings.claim: The focus still names inward favors, while 31:16 makes hiddenness dynamic: even a mustard-weight trace enclosed in a rock or the cosmic domains is brought forth by God, so the inward can also be a scale and location from which the smallest consequential thing remains discloseable and, in the attributed reading, accountable.
findings.mechanism: The focus's inward term meets 31:16's measured weight, tiny seed, hard enclosure, subtle access, and knowledge of an interior; the focus's word for knowledge also meets the context's naming of divine subtlety and awareness. Concealment therefore meets retrieval, changing the inward from a static class of unseen gifts into a domain that remains accessible to divine disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: What is hidden is not thereby beyond divine reach; even minute concealment can remain available for disclosure.
findings.containment: The Arabic of 31:16 says that God brings the tiny item forth. Reading its measured weight as moral accountability and applying the example to the focus's inward favors remain attributed inferences; 31:16 may speak broadly about divine knowledge without revising the focus pair. The connection record also preserves counterevidence that the tiny-object example does not materially clarify the focus's retrieval reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact trace coordinates fit 31:16 and return through focus words, but the extension from hidden trace to the focus's inward favors and accountability remains attributed and has a supplied reciprocal counter-reading.

findings.title: Outward conduct can disclose inward posture
findings.claim: The focus's outward and inward favors can also be read as coupled dimensions: the face, gait, and voice in 31:18-19 make an inward posture inspectable through outward conduct.
findings.mechanism: The focus's outward term names what emerges and its inward term names what is hidden. The context's pride-marked cheek, swaggering walk, and voice supply distinct public surfaces; meeting the pair changes the reading from two separate classes of gift to dimensions that can become legible in a person's use of the body.
findings.reader_payoff: Visible conduct can be read as a surface through which inward measure becomes perceptible.
findings.containment: The inner-to-outer relation is an attributed inference, not a rule that conduct exposes every inner state. The context may remain a set of discrete etiquette instructions; the supplied 31:19 connection note explicitly leaves open whether modest walking and lowering the voice develop the focus's themes.

epistemic.reason: The face, gait, and sound surfaces are supplied, but their interpretation as signals of inward posture is the HFT reader's inference and remains contested by the connection note.

findings.title: An inherited framework can replace the missing standard
findings.claim: While 31:20 describes a disputant without guidance or an illuminating book, 31:21 presents a robust alternative basis: following what was found upon the fathers. The sequence allows an inherited framework to stand where the focus's stated guidance and textual standard are absent.
findings.mechanism: The focus's guidance and book meet the next verse's contrast between following what God sent down and following what people found upon their fathers. The attributed traces for following, finding, and fatherhood identify how a socially received route can become a warrant of its own, changing absence of guidance from no framework into a substitute framework.
findings.reader_payoff: Confidence in a dispute can come from an inherited path even when the focus's named sources of guidance are missing.
findings.containment: The pericope supports a relation between these adjacent descriptions, but it does not establish that the focus's disputant and 31:21's followers are exactly the same people. Nor does the passage make every inherited practice false.

epistemic.reason: The exact 31:21 Arabic directly contrasts revelation with inherited practice, while the word-level HFT root and role annotations remain attributed and the identity link is not established.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The disputant may have a route to follow while lacking the focus's true guidance.
branch_activations.boundary: The relation is contextual and does not identify every inherited path as false.

findings.title: The earlier warning gives the dispute a concrete setting
findings.claim: The warning not to associate partners with God in 31:13 precedes the focus's description of people disputing about God without knowledge or guidance, so the pericope places unsupported argument beside a concrete monotheistic boundary.
findings.mechanism: The earlier command names associating partners with God as grave wrongdoing; the later focus returns to argument about God and specifies its lack of knowledge, guidance, and an illuminating book. Their sequence lets the prior counsel contextualize the later warning without making the focus's unnamed disputants identical to those addressed earlier.
findings.reader_payoff: The later warning can be heard within Luqman's already stated concern about how God is spoken of.
findings.containment: 31:20 does not say that each disputant is committing shirk or that the people in 31:13 and 31:20 are the same group; this is a pericope relation, not an identification.

epistemic.reason: The connection supplies exact 31:13 Arabic and a nearby relation to the focus, but no participant identity or narrower semantic link is established.

findings.title: A directed path can still be destructive
findings.claim: With the focus's true guidance absent, 31:21 supplies a contrasting call: Satan summons people toward punishment. The sequence distinguishes merely having a caller or route from being guided in the right direction.
findings.mechanism: The focus word for guidance carries a right path; the next verse's explicit act of calling toward punishment supplies an independent destructive direction. Their contact changes the absence of guidance from an abstract lack into a warning that direction can be supplied by a harmful call.
findings.reader_payoff: A path is not guidance simply because someone is being led along it.
findings.containment: This is a sequence-level contrast. It does not identify the focus's disputant with 31:21's followers or claim that the focus term for guidance itself names Satan's call.

epistemic.reason: The channel support and exact 31:21 Arabic supply the destructive-call relation, while its return to the focus is contextual and does not settle participant identity.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 31:21 text says Satan calls people toward the blazing punishment.
branch_activations.activation: That destructive call meets the focus's missing true guidance and supplies a counterexample: a direction can be offered without being right guidance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Guidance is not reducible to any route or summons.
branch_activations.boundary: This contrast does not identify the two ayah's audiences or make a general claim about every call to follow.

friction_notes: HFT anchor evidence supplies exact Arabic but no context QAC morphology; its word indices, roots, branches, and roles are retained only as attributed occurrences.

The 31:16 connection preserves counterevidence against using the mustard-weight example to clarify the focus's hidden-benefit reading, and the 31:19 connection leaves open whether conduct advice develops that pair. Both readings remain qualified or exploratory rather than resolved.
